GASTROENTERITIS.title: Gastroenteritis (stomach and bowel infection)

items: Gastroenteritis is an infection of the stomach and bowel, most often from a virus.
It usually clears up on its own within days.
Watery diarrhoea, vomiting, belly cramps, and sometimes fever.
Diarrhoea that lasts less than 14 days is called acute.
Usually no tests are needed for mild illness.
A stool test if symptoms last more than 7 days, if there is blood in the stool, or if you have a weak immune system.
The main treatment is fluid replacement, by mouth or into a vein.
Ask your doctor or pharmacist before using anti-diarrhoea medicine.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Sip fluids often, such as oral rehydration solution.
Wash hands well, and avoid preparing food for others until well.
See your doctor if the diarrhoea is not better after 7 days.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Signs of severe dehydration: very dry mouth, very little urine, dizziness, or fainting
Signs of severe illness, such as fainting
Blood in the stool, or a fast heartbeat
